title: TCU safety Jacob Fields dismissed after allegedly assaulting teammate: Source
content:
TCU’s recent dismissal of projected starting senior safety Jacob Fields stemmed from an alleged assault of a teammate, according to the campus police department and a person familiar with the situation who spoke Thursday on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

Fields, a transfer who was last season’s Conference USA co-Defensive Player of the Year at Louisiana Tech, was dismissed by TCU on Tuesday for a “violation of team rules,” according to the school. Four days prior, on Friday, campus police were called to the TCU athletic facilities for an alleged aggravated assault that happened in the locker room the day prior, according to the crime log.

According to a heavily redacted incident report obtained by The Athletic, TCU’s general manager told the responding officer of an assault that took place in the locker room Aug. 13 at approximately 1:30 p.m. The report characterized the offense as an alleged aggravated assault with hands, feet or fists. The victim’s name and identifying information were redacted except that he was a male. The officer recommended the victim contact police for a more comprehensive report and the possible filing of any charges, if the victim chose to do so.

The alleged assailant was also not identified in the report, but a source familiar with the situation confirmed it was Fields.

A TCU athletics spokesperson declined to comment on the situation. An agent listed on Fields’ social media did not respond to a request for comment. Head coach Sonny Dykes is scheduled to meet with the media Friday morning after practice.

TCU kicks off the season against North Carolina in Dublin on Aug. 29.

The Fort Worth Star-Telegram first reported the news.
